originality.rationale: The new statement is specifically about vertex-membership shattering of two-east-step lattice paths and the sharp first advantage conferred by endpoint queries (b=10). Actual searches of published records for path incidence, intervals, endpoint probes, and adaptive dimension found no statement establishing this first threshold. Primary works read in relevant introductions discuss abstract thicket dimension, learning with equivalence queries, or reachability queries for an unknown graph, not the same concept/query pair. Related mathematical claims on rooted comb paths, cyclic intervals, poset ideals, and window classes have different incidence relations and do not imply the exact endpoint-query threshold. Risk remains from unlocated specialized literature and partial full-text inspection.
residual_risks: Unidentified interval-learning and lattice-path learning literature may contain equivalent statements under other terminology.
Primary papers inspected in selected relevant sections; the complete text of every related publication was not exhaustively examined.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-width northeast path class provides constant VC dimension yet logarithmically unbounded online dimension. The independent structural point is a first nontrivial, sharp query-language threshold: endpoint probes increase online depth at precisely b=10 while not changing the hypotheses or VC dimension. The completely classified finite boundary, general infinite logarithmic bounds, and explicit certificate are useful for comparing static, adaptive and query-language complexity. This is not merely a routine change of notation or a gratuitous parameter.
